sections.h2: Where is Hagerstown, and how did it become the Hub City?
sections.html:
Hagerstown is the seat of Washington County, in western Maryland's Hagerstown Valley between the Blue Ridge and the Allegheny Mountains. It lies about 70 miles northwest of Washington, D.C., and 72 miles west-northwest of Baltimore, just south of the Mason-Dixon line.

Jonathan Hager bought 200 acres in 1739 and founded the town in 1762, naming it Elizabethtown for his wife. It became the county seat around 1776 and was incorporated and renamed Hager's-Town in 1813. The nickname "Hub City" comes from the many railroads that crossed it. Hamilton Run and Antietam Creek, both Potomac tributaries, drain the area, and stone ridges that run northeast to southwest bound some of its neighborhoods.

sections.h2: What does Hagerstown's Civil War past have to do with the town today?
sections.html:
Hagerstown served as a staging area and supply center in four Civil War campaigns, and the legacy shows up in its older housing and in nearby parks. Union troops under Robert Patterson used it as a base in 1861, Longstreet's command occupied it in 1862, and Lee's army passed through in 1863. In July 1864 Confederate cavalry levied a $20,000 ransom on the town.

Antietam National Battlefield, South Mountain, Gettysburg, Monocacy and Harpers Ferry are all within reach, which supports a steady tourism trade. For a seller, the takeaway is practical: many Hagerstown houses are old. Some have original plaster, slate or older flat roofs, and a buyer's inspector will look closely at them.

Hagerstown was historically an industrial town, making railroad equipment, aircraft, trucks, textiles and furniture, and it is now built around logistics, health care and retail. The I-70 and I-81 crossing has drawn warehouses.

  • Healthcare: Meritus Medical Center, the state-run Western Maryland Hospital Center and Brook Lane Psychiatric Center.
  • Retail: Hagerstown Premium Outlets, with more than 100 stores, and Valley Mall.
  • Manufacturing: Hitachi Rail began a $70 million factory in the city, and the former Fairchild plant now makes rifle and pistol ammunition.
  • Logistics, agriculture (dairy, corn, orchards) and tourism.

Kreider-Reisner formed in 1923, merged into Fairchild Aircraft in 1929, and made aircraft components until 1984. The Hagerstown Flying Boxcars, an Atlantic League baseball team, began play at Meritus Park in 2024, and the team name honors that aircraft history. New jobs and a new ballpark can change how buyers see certain streets, but any price effect is a question for an appraiser.

sections.h2: How do roads and the airport affect a Hagerstown sale?
sections.html:
Hagerstown sits where I-70 (east to Baltimore) meets I-81 (north to Pennsylvania and south toward Tennessee), with US 11 and US 40 running parallel to them. That junction is the reason for the warehouse growth and for a large trucking presence.

The city has no passenger rail. CSX, Norfolk Southern and the Winchester and Western Railroad run freight, and the Maryland Transit Administration began a feasibility study in February 2023 on extending the MARC Brunswick line. Hagerstown Regional Airport (Richard A. Henson Field) lies about 5 miles north, where Allegiant Air serves Orlando Sanford, Myrtle Beach and St. Petersburg-Clearwater. Washington County Transit runs local buses.

A commuter who works in the Washington or Baltimore area faces a long drive on I-70 or I-270, while a local worker may be minutes from both interstates. Describe your house's location in those terms when you talk to buyers.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Hagerstown, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Hagerstown has hot, humid summers and cool to moderately cold winters, in a transition zone between humid subtropical and humid continental climates. The normal daily mean is 32.9 degrees F in January and 77.6 degrees F in July.

The record low is minus 27 degrees F, set January 13, 1912, and the record high is 107 degrees F, set July 23, 1999. Wikipedia gives two different figures for annual precipitation, about 39.3 inches in the text and 35.60 inches in the climate table, so treat either as approximate. Winter freeze and thaw cycles are hard on gutters, chimneys and porches, and summer humidity is a common cause of basement moisture. If you have deferred any of that, a buyer purchasing as is will account for it in the price.

sections.h2: Does Hagerstown license rentals and vacant houses?
sections.html:
Yes to both, and the vacant structure rules matter most to anyone selling a house that has stood empty. The city runs a rental licensing program and a separate vacant structure program, both managed by Neighborhood Services.

Rental licensing:

  • Any owner who leases a unit must hold a license, with a nonrefundable annual fee of $75 per unit.
  • Exterior inspections are annual, and interior inspections occur every 48 months at tenant vacancy.
  • Exemptions include owner-plus-one properties, qualifying new construction within four years, and single-unit rentals to close family members, who must still register.

Vacant structure licensing applies to residential buildings vacant for six continuous months, and to residential structures with a pending foreclosure, which the city treats as blighted vacant structures. A structure the city has placarded as uninhabitable for thirty days is also blighted. Exemptions include active work involving two or more systems and the first year of vacancy while the property is listed for sale through a licensed agent. The program was revised most recently on October 28, 2025.

Contact Programs Coordinator Emily McFarland at 301-739-8577 ext. 805 or codecompliance@hagerstownmd.org for fees, deadlines and owner-change forms.

sections.h2: How are property taxes billed and collected in Hagerstown?
sections.html:
Hagerstown property owners get tax bills from two places. The Washington County Treasurer's Office does not collect taxes for the City of Hagerstown, so city taxes come from the city at (301) 790-3200.

The county's annual and first semi-annual installments are due September 30, and the second installment is due December 31. Interest on late payments is 1% per month, and annual and first installments go delinquent on October 1. Paying by July 31 earns a 0.5% discount. The semi-annual option is for owner-occupied primary residences, and mortgage lenders are assumed to pay semi-annually unless you tell the lender before May 1.

The city's real property rate was $1.057 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal 2026, unchanged for the sixth year in a row, according to a local news report on the city budget. SDAT's reassessment report shows Washington County residential values up 22.8% on average between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026, phased in over three years.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes on a Hagerstown house go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county holds a tax lien sale each year, on the first Tuesday in June at 9:00 a.m., at the Washington County Office Building, 35 West Washington Street, Hagerstown. The sale puts the lien up, not the house itself.

Delinquency notices go out around March 1, and the accounts are advertised weekly for four weeks. Owners can redeem until a court decree ends the right. The redemption amount is the sale price, 6% annual interest from the sale date and any new taxes. After four months, the buyer of the lien can add legal fees. At settlement, the settlement attorney collects any unpaid taxes, because all real estate taxes must be current before the deed can transfer.

If you are behind, call the Treasurer's Office at 240-313-2110 to confirm the exact amount before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: What do Hagerstown sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Hagerstown sellers most often deal with houses that have aged, been empty or been rented, and the city's license rules apply to all three.

  • A house empty for six months that may need a vacant structure license.
  • A rental with a license and inspection history to check.
  • Back taxes, a lien or a tax sale notice to clear at settlement.
  • Older construction with deferred repairs.
  • Maryland's disclosure or disclaimer form, which sellers of one-to-four unit homes must provide, with a 5-day rescission right for the buyer if it arrives late.

faqs.q: Does Hagerstown require a license for a vacant house?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. Residential structures vacant for six continuous months must be licensed, and a house with a pending foreclosure is treated as blighted. A first year of vacancy while listed with a licensed agent is exempt.

faqs.q: How much is a rental license in Hagerstown?
faqs.a: The annual fee is $75 per rental unit. Exterior inspections are annual and interior inspections happen every 48 months at tenant vacancy.

faqs.q: Does the Washington County Treasurer collect Hagerstown city taxes?
faqs.a: No. City taxes are collected by the City of Hagerstown, reachable at (301) 790-3200. The county bills the county portion.

faqs.q: When is the Washington County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county holds its tax lien sale on the first Tuesday in June at 9:00 a.m. The sale is of the lien, not the property.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Washington County?
faqs.a: The Department of Legislative Services table lists a 0.5% county transfer tax. How the cost is split between buyer and seller is set in the contract.
